selectedOriginals.caption: Palacio Nacional de Sintra from above
selectedOriginals.inspection: Full2019 elevated local original inspected: four actual pointed front arcade spans below paired upper windows, broad front stair/raised fountain terrace and curved balustrades, two lower front flanking masses, polygonal/offset range arrangement, red clay roofs, white serrated/parapet trim and yellow corner strips. Manueline wing has six richly framed paired openings and adjoining two-level triple-arch loggia. Rear Coats-of-Arms tower, west terraces/pergola and twin white kitchen chimneys. Town buildings, plants, cranes, people and vehicles excluded.

additionalInspected.caption: The National Palace of Sintra, Portugal, view from east.
additionalInspected.inspection: Full2015 east exterior original inspected: paired conical white chimneys with two collar transitions near each narrow open mouth; massive lower Manueline basement/recessed door/window storeys step down the slope. Two main ornamental window levels, two three-arch open loggias and serrated white roof-edge battlements. Main front and rear lower roof ranges are distinct, not a single rectangular palace block.

additionalInspected.caption: Manueline wing of the National Palace of Sintra, Portugal
additionalInspected.inspection: Full2015 Manueline wing original inspected: exactly three paired carved window groups on each of two principal levels; small square basement lights, three small rounded ground doors, warm ochre vertical corner strips, projecting serrated white parapets, adjoining2x3 open round arches on Tuscan columns and smaller middle light. Left connecting passage and actual external stair/porch support. Original restrained geometric stone/leaf detail should replace literal heraldry/figures.

additionalInspected.caption: Palácio Nacional de Sintra, Portugal. Main courtyard
additionalInspected.inspection: Full2015 Patim/courtyard original inspected: actual raised landing and straight descending stone flight, black iron railing, two slender stone porch columns supporting a small tiled roof, real ogee doorway and paired cusp-headed lights. Green/cream geometric tile dado and denser multicolour geometric portal tile field; no photographed facade textures. This photo is labelled main courtyard generically, but local Commons categories call it Patim; do not identify it as all of the Central Patio.

additionalInspected.caption: Sintra 02
additionalInspected.inspection: Full local paired-window original inspected: deeply layered rectangular stone surrounds, two cusp/scallop-headed arches per pair, slender central and twisted side columns, brown wood frames and transparent/opaque glazing, small black iron balcony rail on one bay and tiled roof eave/corbel rhythm. Useful close exterior detail, not an interior scene.

additionalInspected.caption: Palácio Nacional de Sintra‎ in Sintra in Portugal
additionalInspected.inspection: Full local front-terrace original inspected: real two-tier stone fountain/basin, pierced stone balustrade and finials, irregular stone paving, own raised landing and broad stairs down to the town square. Surrounding town buildings are context only; ground and retaining heights still need independent field evidence.

additionalInspected.caption: New Years 2010/2011
additionalInspected.inspection: Full older local western terrace original inspected: layered lower and taller rear white/yellow ranges, red clay tiled slopes, three varied paired upper cusp/ogee windows, simple lower rectangular stone-framed lights, iron railing at intermediate terrace, rounded drain opening and stone balustrade/retaining levels. Dark biological weathering is dated evidence and should not be mistaken for a current uniformly stained finish.

scope: Main palace ranges, courts and twin conical kitchen chimneys; exclude town buildings and palace interiors.
limitations: No source model, runtime asset, final map frame, heightfield, placement proposal, QA approval or story completion annotation has been created for this target. Counts remain73 ready/79 authored/79 started.
Operator33m height is kitchen floor to chimney top; all other vertical dimensions must be explicit proportional estimates.
Dated exterior finish/roof/threshold details differ across references; current2026 chapel conservation is not reflected in2015/2019 images.
Owner page9 is a visitor illustration; no claim of measured construction drawings. Independent ground must precede geometry.

Native main building has six inner rings: four actual mapped open courts/lightwells and two circular kitchen chimney boundaries. The latter are occupied by modeled chimneys, not extra courtyards. Scope also retains the separate native western terrace entry range, southwest front-flanking mass, northeast porch connection and own retaining/terrace structure; town buildings are excluded.

Actual aerial/owner overview place the four pointed main front spans on the southeast-facing native edge14→13. The west outline is not the main arcade. +X follows this facade toward the Manueline wing; +Z faces the exterior forecourt. Cartographic simplification and dated photos limit precision.

Official July2024 DGT classified LiDAR point observations constrain roof and terrace levels separately from class2 terrain. Class6 returns are not ground; palace-floor levels inferred from class6 surface distributions are dimensional observations, not a surveyed plan. Chimney33m is measured from kitchen floor to top.

Independent public class2 ground is frozen before geometry. There are no class2 returns under most palace roofs/courts: fixed inverse-distance interpolation across these gaps is an independent terrain approximation, not measured subterranean ground. No fitting, flattening or editing to match the building; compatible host terrain is required and default coarse Earth terrain is not certified.
